thread:
sam_w: heads-up — after the quantized reranker bring-up we see NDCG up ~2.5% on the synthetic benchmark but human holdout shows MRR down. Feels like a score-distribution shift, not actual quality gain. anyone else see this? :thinking:

maria_g: saw that too. quick glance: rk-v2-quant produces a tighter high-score cluster, so more docs pass the threshold in synth eval. the synthetic golds are permissive, so bump in NDCG is plausible.

jonathan: +1. can we plot score histograms split by label (pos/neg) and by dataset (synthetic vs human)? also check rank-position deltas per query.

sam_w: yeah i'm running a quick diagnostic now. command i'm using: `python tools/rerank_eval.py --model rk-v2-quant --cohorts synth,human-holdout --dump hist --bins 120`

infra-bot: deploy-qa: evaluation job 1699001255 completed — results at https://internal.reports/rerank/1699001255 (artifacts: histograms, rank_deltas.csv)

maria_g: looking at the histograms, quantized scores have reduced variance and a small positive bias for many queries. negative candidates are pushed up slightly, which inflates NDCG if the synthetic gold labeling has low precision.

yuki: my hypothesis: our synthetic gold generator prefers longer passages and scores them as positives when they contain partial matches. quantized model may be less sensitive to subtle negatives and thus gives those longer passages higher scores. synthetic eval rewards that. human labels penalize it.

chris_h: could also be numeric instability from the final layer quantization (logit scaling). check logits before softmax / temperature. try running a calibration (Platt or isotonic) on a small labeled set and see if MRR aligns.

sam_w: good call. i'm pulling a small random human-labeled slice (n=2k) for calibration. SQL I ran to extract it: ```
SELECT query_id, candidate_id, label, candidate_text
FROM human_labels.rerank_holdout
WHERE split = 'random_2k' AND label IS NOT NULL;
```

jonathan: after that we should re-eval with calibrated scores and recompute NDCG/MRR. also run per-query scatter of (score_base - score_quant) vs doc_length and vs token_overlap. if correlation with length is high -> synthetic golds bias.

maria_g: another quick probe: re-run synth eval but de-dup and clamp candidate lengths: `python tools/rerank_eval.py --model rk-v2-quant --cohort synth --dedupe --max-tokens 512` — see if NDCG bump disappears. if it does, synthetic generation is the likely culprit.

sam_w: i'm on it. starting the clamp run now. ETA ~6m.

chris_h: also try temperature tweak: `--score-temp 0.9` vs `1.0` for quant model, and compare score CDFs. small temp change sometimes undoes the numeric bias.

yuki: if we confirm synthetic bias, propose we: 1) adjust synthetic oracle to penalize partial/long matches, 2) add a small human-labeled calibration fold to the onboarding checklist, 3) block promotion until MRR doesn't regress beyond threshold.

sam_w: agreed on the checklist update. will file a short PR to onboarding docs if the triage confirms.

infra-bot: job 1699001278: clamp run completed, artifacts -> https://internal.reports/rerank/1699001278/histograms

maria_g: early look: clamp removed most of the NDCG delta. quant model NDCG drops back in synth when we dedupe+clamp. looks like synthetic gold noise.

jonathan: ok good. next steps: 1) run calibration on human slice and publish calibrated_metrics, 2) add a quick synth-gold quality check (length/partial-match ratio) to auto-eval, 3) update onboarding checklist to require human holdout check before signoff. i'll take the auto-eval check.

sam_w: thanks all. i'll open the PR and attach the artifacts and commands to reproduce. tagging @product for visibility on the onboarding change. :thumbsup:
